title: Paycheck in 30 seconds: a fast, accurate take-home method
excerpt: A quick way to estimate your net pay with federal, state, and payroll taxes—plus deductions.
author: LockHabit
content:
If you just need a quick, reliable net-pay number, here’s a simple approach that gets you within a few dollars for most situations.

1) Start with gross

Use your pay frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly) and gross pay per period.

Pre-tax deductions

401(k), HSA, commuter—subtract these before income tax.

2) Estimate taxes

Apply effective federal and state rates, then add payroll tax (Social Security + Medicare).

3) Subtract post-tax items

Insurance, garnishments, or other after-tax items.

Pro tip: Open the Income & Taxes calculator for a precise result with sliders and state presets.

title: The 50/30/20 budget—simple, flexible, and realistic
excerpt: A friendly budget that prioritizes needs, funds goals, and still leaves room for wants.
author: LockHabit
content:
The 50/30/20 rule allocates 50% to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings or debt payoff.

Why it works

It’s easy to start and adapts to irregular income.

How to implement

Calculate your monthly take-home. Cap fixed expenses, automate savings, and review quarterly.

title: Rent vs buy in 2025: what the math actually says
excerpt: Rates, taxes, maintenance, opportunity cost—here’s a balanced framework to compare.
author: LockHabit
content:
Buying can build equity, but renting offers flexibility and may cost less after maintenance and taxes.

The key variables

Mortgage rate, property tax, insurance, HOA, repairs, and expected tenure.

Run both scenarios

Compare five- to ten-year totals and invest the difference if renting is cheaper.
